While a demand-response program can shield consumers by issuing financial credits during high-price periods, optimizing this sequential decision-making process presents a unique challenge for reinforcement learning despite the plentiful offline historical smart meter and wholesale pricing data available publicly. Offline historical data fails to capture the dynamic, interactive feedback loop between an electric utility's pricing signals and customer acceptance and adaptation to a demand-response program. To address this, we introduce DR-Gym, an open-source, online Gymnasium-compatible environment designed to train and evaluate demand-response from the electric utility's perspective. Unlike existing device-level energy simulators, our environment focuses on the market-level electric utility setting and provides a rich observational space relevant to the electric utility. The simulator additionally features a regime-switching wholesale price model calibrated to real-world extreme events, alongside physics-based building demand profiles. For our learning signal, we use a configurable, multi-objective reward function for specifying diverse learning objectives. We demonstrate through baseline strategies and data snapshots the capability of our simulator to create realistic and learnable environments.

title: Clouds Determine Diffusion: A Cloud-Deterministic Diffusion Model for Progressive Cloud Removal in Optical Remote Sensing Images
content: Cloud removal is crucial for preprocessing optical remote sensing images affected by natural cloud contamination, which is highly diverse and variable. Clouds of varying thickness often occur simultaneously, where the boundary between these layers is ambiguous and hard to quantitatively define. Consequently, advanced deep learning (DL) techniques, especially diffusion models, have been employed to address complex cloud contamination. They primarily focus on conditional generation and standard Gaussian noise diffusion. Yet this paradigm fails to fully capture the inherent diversity, complexity, and variability of natural cloud contamination, nor does it align with the reconstruction process from severe to mild states, leading to limited generalization in real-world scenes. To overcome these limitations, we propose a cloud-deterministic diffusion and progressive cloud removal (CDPCR) model. It introduces a novel diffusion paradigm where cloud contamination serves as the sole forward degradation source. This allows the model to precisely simulate the morphology and dynamic evolution of real-world cloud contamination, thereby enhancing network exposure to diverse cloud-affected patterns and continuously varying intensities in the training stage. During inference, an enhanced sampler iteratively applies the restoration network and the cloud-deterministic diffusion operator, progressively reversing the cloud degradation while effectively preserving residual details. Leveraging dynamic cloud-driven transitions and iterative updates, CDPCR robustly tackles heterogeneous real-world cloud contamination and achieves more realistic and efficient sequence-to-sequence (S2S) reconstruction for optical time series. Crucially, it operates without requiring external cloud masks while alleviating the strong dependence on clean temporal data. Extensive experiments across different datasets validate the superiority and robustness of the proposed method.
author: Yujun Guo, Wei He, He Huang, Hongyan Zhang

title: Data-Driven Surface Ozone Forecasting Using Node-Based Gated Spatiotemporal Fusion
content: Reliable ground-level ozone ( $\mathrm{O_{3}}$ ) forecasting is critical for mitigating impacts on public health and environmental sustainability and for supporting geoscience- and remote sensing-driven air quality applications. Traditional chemical transport models (CTMs), such as GEOS-Chem, remain widely used; however, their high computational cost and comparatively coarse spatial resolution limit timely, fine-grained guidance. This article introduces spatiotemporal node adaptive fusion (ST-NAF), a framework that integrates a graph attention network (GAT) with Transformer encoders to model intersite spatial relationships and temporal evolution in a unified architecture. Daily  $\mathrm{O_{3}}$  observations from the Tropospheric Ozone Assessment Report (TOAR) dataset for 1999–2017 are used to train an ST-NAF-based model for forecasting. Relative to GEOS-Chem, the ST-NAF-based model reduces prediction bias by 55.61% in rural areas, 55.99% in suburban areas, and 55.90% in urban areas, while improving computational efficiency for large-scale forecasting. Using the United States subset of the global TOAR dataset of daily  $\mathrm{O_{3}}$  ppb (parts per billion) from 1999 to 2017, the model ingests 30-day site histories, constructs distance-informed graph edges, and forecasts site-level  $\mathrm{O_{3}}$  concentrations, achieving the above bias reductions versus GEOS-Chem with lower compute. The compact design enables deployment in low-resource environments and provides a practical, data-driven complement to remote sensing-oriented ozone assessment and decision support.
author: Mohammadreza Akbari Lor, Shaian Khan, Shu-Ching Chen, Mei-Ling Shyu, Amy Christiansen

title: Saccadic Phased Array Radar Sampling of Severe Weather Phenomena—Case Study: A Microburst Event
content: Phased array radars (PARs) provide rapid electronic beam steering that overcomes the mechanical constraints of conventional weather radars, offering new opportunities to observe rapidly evolving phenomena with higher temporal and spatial resolution. This beam agility enables dynamic sampling of storm structures and evolution, supporting adaptive and targeted observations of regions of interest (ROIs). Fully exploiting these capabilities, however, requires adaptive algorithms that can intelligently allocate radar resources. The Saccadic PAR Sampling (SPARS) algorithm addresses this need by emulating key mechanisms of human vision. By integrating peripheral vision (PV), foveal vision (FV), and smooth pursuit (SP), SPARS autonomously identifies ROIs and reallocates beam time, dedicating most of it to targeted observations. This approach provides continuous Lagrangian perspectives and enhances the data quality by maximizing the dwell time. The SPARS algorithm was operated on the SKYLER-I X-band PAR to observe a convective system that produced multiple microbursts over Long Island, NY, on August 13, 2023. This algorithm successfully detected and tracked individual storm cells, capturing the full life cycle of a wet microburst and associated dynamical signatures. Comparisons with operational radar scans highlight the advantages of SPARS-enabled PAR in resolving fine-scale structures and the evolution of rapidly evolving phenomena.
author: Kwonil Kim, Edward Luke, Mariko Oue, Pavlos Kollias

title: Marine Remote Sensing Object Detection in Complex Backgrounds Based on Diffusion Models and Multidirectional Spatial Attention
content: Rapid red-tide detection and ship target extraction in nearshore remote sensing images are important for marine ecological monitoring and maritime management. However, nearshore images are easily affected by marine weather conditions and sensor imaging processes, often suffering from cloud cover and stripe noise. These interferences introduce distracting pseudofeatures and weaken target–background discriminability, limiting the stability and robustness of existing detectors. Moreover, the limited number of difficult samples under such interference further increases detection difficulty in complex nearshore scenes. To address these issues, we construct the nearshore complex-scene marine remote sensing dataset (NCSMRS), which contains 1369 images covering three typical nearshore scene types: cloud cover, stripe noise, and clean background, with bounding-box annotations for marine targets. We further propose the diffusion-augmented multidirectional attention detection framework (DMA-Det). DMA-Det adopts layout-guided diffusion augmentation to enrich difficult training samples and introduces a semantic-edge quality filter (SEQF) to improve the reliability of synthetic data through semantic consistency validation and edge quality filtering. In addition, a multidirectional spatial attention (MDSA) module is designed in the detection network to model axial and nonaxial spatial dependencies and recalibrate multiscale features, thereby enhancing target-aware feature representations and suppressing interference from complex backgrounds. Extensive experiments on NCSMRS show that DMA-Det outperforms representative detectors and achieves stable performance across different nearshore scenes, with  $\mathrm {mAP}_{50}$  and  $\mathrm {mAP}_{50\text {-}95}$  scores of 76.2% and 49.7%, respectively.
author: Zhuowei Wang, Chengzhong Lin, Xingming Liao, Ning Chen, Xingda Chen, Jinyue Chen, Shuisen Chen

title: Accounting for Sea Surface Wind Variability in the Ocean Calibration of Ocean Surface Current Airborne Radar (OSCAR)
content: Airborne flight campaigns are essential to evaluate the performance of new ocean remote sensing radars before launch. However, the accurate calibration of airborne radars is quite challenging due to the limited amount of experimental data and the impact of small-scale wind variability. For example, during the flight experiments of the ocean surface current airborne radar (OSCAR), the conventional ocean calibration (OC) shows up to 4-dB difference between the calibration curves from different flight legs. One possible reason for such inconsistency is small-scale wind variability captured by OSCAR but not by the reference winds. As such, this article proposes a new OC method to effectively address both the first-order backscattering bias and the inherent wind variability simultaneously. The calibration technique and wind retrieval are integrated into an iterative framework, thus ensuring that the calibration results are converging and self-consistent. Then, verification against spaceborne scatterometer winds proves that the proposed calibration strategy generally leads to higher quality leg-mean wind retrievals than the conventional OC. Finally, the feasibility of retrieving high spatial resolution wind data from OSCAR test flights is evaluated. As expected, OSCAR can capture finer small-scale wind variations compared to both numerical models and scatterometers, thus offering high-quality wind data for fine-scale research and applications.
author: Wenming Lin, Xiaoheng Mou, Marcos Portabella, Giuseppe Grieco, David L. McCann, Adrien C. H. Martin

title: An Urban Single-Channel Algorithm for Retrieving Land Surface Temperature From Chinese ZY1-02E Data
content: Urban land surface temperature (ULST) is a key parameter for characterizing urban thermal environments and surface energy processes. However, the satellite-based ULST retrieval remains constrained by the coarse spatial resolution of conventional thermal infrared (TIR) sensors. The Chinese ZY1-02E satellite provides a unique opportunity for fine-scale thermal observation with its 15-m resolution TIR sensor (IRS), but its broadband spectral response (7– $12~\mu $ m) challenges the atmospheric assumptions underlying conventional mono-window algorithms. In this study, an urban single-channel (USC) algorithm is developed for retrieving land surface temperature (LST) from ZY1-02E IRS data. Unlike traditional mono-window approaches designed for narrow atmospheric-window sensors, the proposed method explicitly considers the broadband spectral characteristics of IRS and separately characterizes the upward and downward atmospheric radiative contributions in the surface–atmosphere radiation transfer process. The algorithm was evaluated against in situ measurements and cross-compared with satellite-derived LST products and existing single-channel (SC) methods. The results show that the proposed USC algorithm achieves mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean square error (RMSE) of 1.65 and 2.31 K, respectively, outperforming the Qin_SC and JM_SC algorithms. Cross-validation with Landsat 8 LST products demonstrates consistent spatial patterns over both urban and natural surfaces, with MAEs of 1.75 and 2.09 K, respectively. Furthermore, the comparisons with other USC algorithms show that the USC algorithm achieves the lowest retrieval errors. The proposed framework provides a physically based approach for LST retrieval from broadband TIR observations and facilitates high-resolution characterization of urban thermal environments.
author: Qi Zhang, Kun Li, Mengshuo Chen, Qiangyi Yu, Yonggang Qian

title: Identifying Seismogenic Anomalies in Satellite Microwave Emissions by Decoupling Environmental Confounders via Physics-Informed Deep Learning
content: Identifying reliable microwave emission anomalies related to impending earthquakes (EQs) remains challenging due to their intricate coupling with surface environmental dynamics. While previous studies rely heavily on historical baselines to remove background emissions, they largely overlook the terrestrial confounding factors inherent within the seismic influence period, compromising the reliability of obtained anomalies. To bridge this gap, we present a novel microwave-physics-informed deep learning (DL) framework that captures the spatiotemporal dependencies of satellite observations across both historical baselines and concurrent influence periods. Distinct from purely data-driven approaches, we embed explicit microwave physical constraints—namely, dual-polarization consistency and gradient monotonicity—directly into the loss function. Validated across multiple EQ cases, our model effectively decouples overwhelming meteorological and surface interferences (e.g., soil moisture variations, precipitation) from the microwave observations, isolating residuals highly associated with targeted EQs. Comparative analysis demonstrates the framework’s superiority over traditional techniques, achieving an average 22% increase in contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) and a 260% enhancement in average anomaly intensity. Ablation studies further confirm that microwave physical constraints significantly enhance reconstruction fidelity, improving the correlation coefficient by 3% and reducing root-mean-square error (RMSE) by 36%. Crucially, validation against ancillary datasets reveals that our framework can account for nonseismic drivers. Consequently, the derived residuals are largely immune to these confounders and inherently seismogenic, substantially reducing the need for post-hoc exclusion analyses. This work provides a physically interpretable solution for identifying reliable seismic precursors using multisource satellite remote sensing, bearing profound implications for the future development of an operational, precursor-based EQ forecasting framework.
author: Yuan Qi, Bo Huang, Min Zhao, Pan Xiong, Ying Zhang, Wenfei Mao, Lixin Wu

title: Physics-Aware Feature Calibration Network for Remote Sensing Image Segmentation
content: In remote sensing image segmentation, regions with sharp intensity variations caused by complex illumination and ground objects significantly constrain segmentation accuracy. Most existing methods attempt to enhance the model’s perception of these regions by introducing frequency features or relying on spatial convolutions. However, these methods tend to capture signal intensity, exhibiting limitations in distinguishing between sharp shadows and object edges in remote sensing images, which share similar intensities but stem from distinct physical origins. Through theoretical analysis, we observe that real edges typically exhibit an anisotropic gradient distribution, whereas shadow edges tend to show pseudoisotropic local gradient statistics under texture perturbations. To this end, we propose physics-aware feature calibration network (PAFCNet). The physics calibration module (PCM) introduces a GLRT-inspired differentiable decision mechanism to transform the anisotropy analysis of local gradient second moment into a learnable statistical decision process, thereby adaptively enhancing the generalizability of theoretical analysis in real-world scenes. In parallel, the frequency analysis module (FAM) constructs multidirectional object representations via affine transformations (ATs) and parameterized kernel functions (PKFs), while filtering out the interference of sharp shadows through the PCM. Finally, the dual domain fusion module (DFM) performs cross-sequence interaction between the physics-rectified frequency features and spatial features, thereby alleviating the semantic ambiguity associated with single-domain features. Experimental results demonstrate that PAFCNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods. The source code is available at https://github.com/wangjunyi-1/PAFCN
author: Junyi Wang, Guodong Fan, Linwei Fan, Jinjiang Li, Yakun Ju, Alex C. Kot

title: SAM-STIR: Detection-Guided Memory Update for SAM 3-Based Infrared Small and Tiny Object Tracking
content: Infrared small and tiny object tracking plays an important role in security surveillance, remote sensing, and military applications. The vision foundation-model segment anything model (SAM) 3 demonstrates strong tracking capability through a cooperative verification mechanism between its detector and tracker, yet its performance degrades substantially on infrared small and tiny targets. We identify tracker-drift-induced memory collapse as a central failure mode: for small and tiny infrared targets, drifted self-propagated masks can be repeatedly written into the memory bank, gradually turning a reliable temporal prior into a source of self-reinforcing errors. To counter this memory collapse, we propose SAM-STIR, a SAM 3-based infrared tracking framework centered on detection-guided memory update. Instead of relying on the tracker itself as the memory-update source, SAM-STIR refreshes memory with matched high-confidence detector masks, thereby reducing drift-induced memory contamination. To make this update reliable for small and tiny targets, we introduce a normalized distance-based matching mechanism as a geometric matching gate before memory reconditioning. We further employ a lightweight spatio-temporal differential aggregation (STDA) front-end to provide infrared contour and motion cues for subsequent matching and propagation. Experiments on the CST antiuncrewed aerial vehicles (UAV) and Anti-UAV 410 datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves the best mSA among the compared methods, reaching 62.63% and 69.41%, respectively, and outperforming the fine-tuned SAM 3 baseline by 9.43 and 4.59 percentage points.
author: Xiao Hu, Yun Zhou, Jian Lv, Wenjie Lai, Yadong Jiang

title: Dynamic Spectral Graph Wavelet Transform and Iterative Reweighted Physical Residual Feedback for Infrared Small Target Detection
content: Infrared small target detection (IRSTD) in heterogeneous and dynamic environments remains challenging because evolving clutter structures may produce sparse responses similar to those of genuine targets. Existing tensor robust principal component analysis (TRPCA) methods mainly separate the background and target by exploiting global low-rank properties and element-wise sparsity. However, a single global low-rank component may not adequately represent weak and locally organized background variations. These variations can remain in the residual and contaminate the estimated target component. To address this limitation, we innovatively shift the IRSTD paradigm from the traditional spatial domain to the spectral graph wavelet domain, proposing a target detection model combining dynamic spectral graph wavelet transform and iterative reweighted physical residual feedback (DSGWT-IRFR). Specifically, the model constructs a heat diffusion graph filter to capture the underlying nonstationary clutter manifold, and derives orthogonal graph-spectral decoupling operators via a Bessel–Chebyshev expansion. Leveraging these decoupling operators, we design a cross-band nuclear norm regularization for the background manifold to independently regulate the low-frequency global base and high-frequency local edges, thereby cutting off structural leakage pathways. Concurrently, we impose a polarized graph-spectral constraint on the target residual. By eradicating low-frequency cloud false alarms via extreme penalization and coupling the high-frequency spectrum with a morphological topology-driven iterative reweighted physical residual feedback (IRFR) mechanism, our model mathematically and rigorously decouples genuine target singularities from severe clutter. Extensive experiments across eight challenging scenarios demonstrate that the proposed DSGWT-IRFR exhibits highly competitive overall performance compared with 11 state-of-the-art baselines, achieving significant advantages in signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and threshold robustness [3-D receiver operating characteristic (ROC)]. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/w-a-q/DSGWT-IRFR
author: Anqing Wu, Qiang Guo, Mykola Kaliuzhnyi

title: DualSight-Fire: A Cognitive Dual-Decoder Network for Robust Fire Segmentation in Multispectral Remote Sensing Images
content: Small fire segmentation in remote sensing imagery is a critical yet challenging task due to the extreme foreground–background imbalance and the interference from complex background clutter. To this end, we propose a novel dual-decoder network, DualSight-Fire, to accurately detect small fire spots. The proposed method consists of a segmentation decoder and a reconstruction decoder. The reconstruction branch incorporates a contextual background modeling block (CBMB) to explicitly model background features and capture long-range dependencies. To enhance the discriminability of fire targets, a feature discrepancy fusion module is proposed to suppress background noise by exploiting the discrepancy between the segmentation and reconstruction features. Moreover, we propose a spatial-focal loss (SFL), which dynamically weights flame regions based on their area and shape, thereby achieving targeted learning optimization for tiny targets and boundary information. Extensive experiments on the Active Fire and Land8Fire datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches, obtaining the highest  $F1$ -score and IoU. The code is available at https://github.com/HIAS-Zhao/fire-segmentation
author: Guozhen He, Hongyi Chen, Yuanye Ma, Yaoqi Liu, Hao Zhou, Di Gao, Yuhua Zheng, Haining Tan, Yaoqi Bao, Yinhe Han, Jianyu Wang, Yisheng Zhao

title: S2-SFDA: Spatial-Selective Information Filter-Driven for Source-Free Cross-Domain Infrared Small Target Detection
content: Infrared small target detection (IRSTD) plays a critical role in applications, e.g., counter-UAV surveillance and long-range early warning. However, acquiring and annotating real infrared datasets is expensive and labor-intensive. As a result, previous works mainly train on synthetic data and test on unseen real-world images, resulting in a significant domain shift. While unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) can mitigate this issue, it often requires access to source data, which is impractical in real-world scenarios. To address this issue, we propose a novel source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) framework, namely S2-SFDA, to mitigate domain discrepancies while preserving weak target responses for synthetic-to-real IRSTD. S2-SFDA has three key components. Specifically, we first design a spatial-selective block-wise DCT information filter (SSDF) to suppress domain-specific information (DSI). Then, an information bottleneck (IB)-constrained domain-invariant representation learning (IBDR) is proposed to eliminate redundant features and promote transferable representations. Furthermore, we develop a multilevel pseudo-label self-supervised learning (MLPL) strategy to provide stable supervision during adaptation. Finally, extensive experiments and comparisons are conducted on multiple IRSTD benchmarks. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed S2-SFDA shows promising performance and surpasses both classical and state-of-the-art methods.
author: Ke Li, Fujun Han, Yining Wang, Kewen Huang, Bowen Duan, Yan Tian

title: A Novel Scene-Aware Pipeline Architecture for Spaceborne SAR Regional Imaging and Ship Target Detection
content: With the rapid advancement of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) technology and the explosive growth of on-orbit data, conventional processing frameworks are increasingly constrained by high resource consumption and substantial latency, rendering them inadequate for real-time maritime ship detection on resource-limited platforms. To address this challenge, this article proposes a novel scene-aware imaging-detection integration (SAIDI) architecture for stripmap-mode SAR, which unifies traditionally decoupled imaging and detection tasks into a cascaded processing pipeline. Specifically, the framework comprises four key components: an imaging necessity judgment module to filter target-free raw echoes, a fast imaging algorithm bypassing range cell migration correction, a lightweight pruned YOLOv11 detection network, and a dedicated ship dataset constructed from real satellite measurements. Experiments on real satellite data demonstrate that the proposed method maintains robust detection performance in both open-ocean and coastal scenarios while eliminating redundant computations in background regions. Compared to conventional methods, the proposed scheme significantly reduces processing latency and peak memory footprint, while optimizing CPU utilization and power efficiency. In addition, this method is mainly designed for medium- and large-sized marine ships.
author: Yueming Sun, Wei Yang, Hongcheng Zeng, Xiaojie Zhou, Guanhe Lin, Luhao Wang, Yuang Li, Yamin Wang, Yikui Zhai, Wei Xiong, Jie Chen

title: Multigranularity Spatial-Frequency Cross-Modal Correlation Paradigm for Pan-Sharpening
content: Pan-sharpening aims to generate high-resolution multispectral (HRMS) images by integrating geometric details from panchromatic (PAN) imagery with the spectral characteristics of low-resolution MS data. The fundamental challenge lies in effectively modeling cross-modal interactions across both spatial and spectral domains. While transformer-based methods have shown potential by employing self-attention within local windows to capture cross-modal dependencies, these approaches often suffer from limited receptive fields and high computational complexity. To overcome these limitations, this article introduces a novel multigranularity spatial-frequency cross-modal correlation paradigm for pan-sharpening. The proposed method utilizes the DCT followed by a local nonoverlapping window partitioning scheme to explicitly decompose both PAN and MS images into multigranularity frequency components. This transformation yields a structured and disentangled representation where low-frequency coefficients encode coarse structural content and high-frequency coefficients capture fine textural details. Each frequency token inherently embodies nonlocal characteristics, thereby providing a global receptive field within the frequency domain. Cross-modal correlation is computed by treating MS features as queries and PAN features as keys and values, with self-attention applied within each discrete frequency band across windows. This design not only preserves global contextual information within each frequency token but also significantly enhances interaction across different frequency bands. Furthermore, we introduce a spatial filtering modulation mechanism to work complementarily to the frequency-domain attention by filtering out irrelevant features and strengthening cross-modal feature integration. This module works synergistically with the frequency-domain attention by selectively emphasizing relevant features and suppressing noise, thereby improving cross-scale feature integration. Extensive experimental results over multiple satellite benchmarks validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.
author: Wenyang Zhou, Jiangtao Cui, Gang Yang, Xiaofang Xia, Man Zhou, Xuanhua He, Yuan Zhou, Danfeng Hong

title: SPVP-Net: Structural Prior-Driven Deep Unfolding Network for Pansharpening
content: To effectively characterize the similarity between multispectral (MS) and panchromatic (PAN) images while optimally balancing spectral and spatial fidelity in fusion results, this article proposes a spectral–spatial joint fidelity and structural prior-driven deep unfolding network for pansharpening. We formulate a variational optimization model integrating two key components: a spectral–spatial joint fidelity term derived from the detail injection framework, and a structural similarity prior regularization term leveraging a deep structural feature operator. The model optimization is decomposed into two subproblems, detail injection and structure correction, which are transformed into corresponding subnetworks via algorithm unfolding. A deep neural network for pansharpening is subsequently designed based on this solution process. Critically, all parameters and operators are jointly learned within the network, eliminating the need for manual parameter selection inherent in traditional variational methods. This approach synergizes the explicit physical interpretability of variational models with the capacity of deep networks to model complex nonlinear relationships. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to state-of-the-art pansharpening methods, the proposed method demonstrates significant gains in preserving geometric structures through exploitation of PAN-MS structural similarity.
author: Zhikang Xiang, Yu Shen, Jingxiang Yang, Liang Xiao

title: Spectral–Spatiotemporal Prompting for Multispectral UAV Tracking
content: UAV tracking often faces critical challenges such as target appearance variations and poor lighting conditions. Compared to RGB images, multispectral images (MSIs) possess rich spatial–spectral information, enabling trackers to better handle scenarios involving illumination variations and similar colors. Existing multispectral (MS) tracking methods typically rely on full fine-tuning of RGB-based models and inadequately exploit temporal information, leading to suboptimal performance due to limited training data. To address these issues, we propose a unified spectral–spatiotemporal prompting (SSTP) for MS UAV tracking, named SSTP. We design a dual-granularity spatial–spectral fusion ( $\mathbf {DGS^{2}F}$ ) module to extract and fuse coarse-grained spatial features and fine-grained spectral features, enabling more comprehensive utilization of detailed spectral information. Furthermore, we introduce hierarchical temporal modeling, where short-term memory prompt (SMP) enhances the backbone network for joint spectral–spatiotemporal feature extraction, while Mamba-based long-term memory prompt (MLMP) facilitates long-range motion sequence modeling. Extensive experiments on the MS tracking benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance while maintaining real-time efficiency, with separate training and evaluation conducted on each benchmark, achieving an AUC of 69.2% on the MUST dataset and leading performance on both the HOT2020 and HOT2024 datasets. The code will be available at https://github.com/YXYbit/SSTP
author: Xiaoyue Yan, Tingfa Xu, Haolin Qin, Tianhao Li, Jianan Li

title: AgriSafeNet: Leveraging RGB-TIR UAV Remote Sensing Imagery for Transmission Line Detection in Smart Agriculture
content: In modern smart agriculture, the uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) have emerged as indispensable low-altitude remote sensing platforms, particularly for precision irrigation and crop protection. While they enable the efficient acquisition of high-resolution spatial information and significantly enhance agricultural productivity, UAVs operating in complex environments face severe collision risks with power infrastructure, which poses a substantial threat to flight safety. Consequently, robust transmission line detection (TLD) is a critical prerequisite for ensuring safe autonomous UAV navigation. Despite the importance of this task, the existing detection methods often exhibit limitations in modeling fine-grained structural characteristics and fail to effectively integrate cross-modal contextual information. To address these challenges, this article proposes AgriSafeNet, a novel RGB-TIR TLD framework designed to bolster feature representation and multimodal fusion. Specifically, AgriSafeNet orchestrates efficient shallow-level cross-modal interaction through a multiscale feature decoupling and fusion module (MFDFM). Furthermore, it refines deep semantic integration via a spatial compression attention fusion module (SCAFM) and incorporates a context-guided feature extraction module (CGFEM) to capture intricate structural geometric details. This hierarchical design significantly improves the discriminability of transmission line (TL) features and the robustness of the model against environmental interference. Extensive experiments conducted on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that AgriSafeNet achieves the state-of-the-art performance, consistently outperforming the existing methods in complex agricultural scenarios.
author: Yichen Liu, Wenxuan Zhang, Xuanrui Chen, Zhao Ma, Junjie Ye, Guo Zheng, Lijie Wang, Wei Hou

title: D3A-Net: A Deformable 3-D Attention Network for Hyperspectral Unmixing
content: Hyperspectral unmixing (HU) aims to decompose mixed pixels into endmember spectra and corresponding abundance maps under physically interpretable constraints. Despite recent progress in convolutional neural network (CNN)- and Transformer-based approaches, most existing methods still rely on rigid sampling grids or process spatial and spectral features separately, which may cause feature misalignment for irregular and elongated structures and weaken spectral–spatial volumetric continuity. To address these limitations, we propose a deformable 3-D attention network (D3A-Net), a fully 3-D U-shaped encoder–decoder that processes hyperspectral imagery as a unified data cube and overcomes the constraints of fixed receptive fields. D3A-Net is constructed by stacking 3D-DeFormer blocks (3D-DFBs), each of which incorporates a 3-D multiscale deformable neighbourhood-attention (MS-DNA) module and a complementary local extraction branch, followed by a gated feed-forward module for efficient feature transformation. The physics-guided unmixing Encoder II enforces the abundance nonnegativity and sum-to-one constraints, while the linear decoder reconstructs the hyperspectral image (HSI), enabling end-to-end unsupervised learning. Extensive experiments on a synthetic dataset under multiple signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) settings and three real-world datasets (Samson, Jasper Ridge, and APEX) demonstrate that D3A-Net achieves accurate endmember estimation and abundance estimation.
author: Fanqiang Kong, Haocheng Yang, Zhibo Wu, Tongshu Wu, Yunsong Li

title: UHFusion: Prompt-Guided Multi-Task Learning Network for Hyperspectral Image Fusion via Multi-Type Mixture-of-Experts
content: Hyperspectral image (HSI) fusion aims to generate high-resolution HSI by integrating low-resolution hyperspectral data with auxiliary high-resolution sources (e.g., panchromatic (PAN), RGB, or MSI). While recent deep learning-based HSI fusion approaches have achieved promising results, they are typically designed for specific modality pairs and struggle to generalize across diverse fusion settings, leading to redundant architectures and limited adaptability. To overcome these limitations, we propose UHFusion, a prompt-guided multi-task learning (MTL) network for HSI fusion, which enables flexible multi-task adaptation within a single framework. Particularly, UHFusion introduces two key components: 1) a multi-type mixture-of-experts (MTMoEs) that decomposes HSI fusion into complementary spatial, spectral, and spatial–spectral reasoning processes, and dynamically composes expert responses conditioned on the auxiliary modality, allowing the model to selectively emphasize task-relevant spatial structures or spectral characteristics without architectural modification; and 2) a prompt-guided multi-task adaptation module (PMAM), which encodes modality-specific priors into learnable prompt embeddings and leverages a task relation graph to perform task-conditioned feature modulation, thereby improving the spatial–spectral fusion quality across diverse fusion tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that UHFusion achieves superior performance and generalization across multiple HSI fusion tasks and modalities, providing an effective all-in-one solution for HSI reconstruction. The code is available at: https://github.com/Jiahuiqu/UHFusion
author: Shaoxiong Hou, Jiahui Qu, Wenqian Dong, Yunsong Li

title: Transition-Aware Boundary-Guided Dual-Frequency Network for Hyperspectral Unmixing
content: Hyperspectral unmixing (HU) aims to decompose mixed pixels into endmembers and their corresponding abundances. However, material transition zones often suffer from severe spectral mixing and error diffusion, making abundance estimation particularly brittle near boundaries. To substantiate this claim, we first formulate and validate a boundary–transition prior through a testable hypothesis. High-frequency (HF) responses extracted from observed hyperspectral images (HSIs) consistently align with material boundaries. Quantitative alignment evidence on synthetic data (with abundance ground truth) and real scenes (using structural boundary proxies) supports this prior. Building on this validated prior, we propose a transition-aware boundary-guided dual-frequency network for HU. A stationary wavelet transform (SWT) decomposes the HSI into low-frequency (LF) and HF components that are modeled by dual branches, while a learnable boundary-guidance map predicted from the HF branch adaptively fuses dual-frequency representations to refine transition regions without imposing explicit spatial smoothness regularization. A lightweight global guidance pathway further enriches spectral–spatial context. Experiments on synthetic and real datasets demonstrate that the proposed TABG-Net significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, especially in preserving sharp boundaries and producing accurate abundances in transition-dominated scenarios. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/hgxcxdg/TABG-Net
author: Yaxiong Chen, Siqi Liang, Quanchuan Cheng, Bo Zhang, Shengwu Xiong, Xiaoqiang Lu

title: EGAS-Net: Entropy-Guided Adaptive Selection Network for Hyperspectral–LiDAR Classification
content: The complementarity of hyperspectral imagery (HSI) and light detection and ranging (LiDAR) data provides significant advantages in land-cover classification. In current methods, the cropping size is typically determined by empirical selection, which readily results in the redundancy or loss of land-cover feature statistics. Information entropy, a key measure of data uncertainty and richness, plays a crucial role in selecting feature channels with abundant texture cues and strong discriminability. Motivated by this, this article proposes an entropy-guided adaptive selection network (EGAS-Net) for hyperspectral–LiDAR classification. With information entropy as the core, this method adaptively selects the optimal size for each land cover by calculating spatial information entropy and spatial–spectral information entropy to maximize information content. Then, the spatial and frequency information entropies of HSI and LiDAR data are obtained after cropping. Adaptive weighting is implemented based on the information content ratio of each entropy feature to establish a cross-modal spatial–frequency information interaction mechanism. During the feature fusion stage, the final features are generated through entropy feature weighted coupling to fully exploit the complementary value of HSI–LiDAR data. Experimental results on the Houston 2013, MUUFL, Augsburg, and Yancheng datasets show that the proposed method outperforms other empirical size-based networks, achieving higher classification scores. The code of this project will be available at https://github.com/ZhaoYuQing01/EGASNet
author: Yuqing Zhao, Yu Song, Chao Liang, Kang Ni, Peng Wang

title: Multimodal Cross-Scene Hyperspectral Image Classification Guided by Dual-Agent Priori Knowledge
content: Semantic information is increasingly used to improve the performance of cross-scene hyperspectral image (HSI) classification. However, existing methods have difficulty fully exploiting the prior knowledge of large language models (LLMs) in textual information and usually rely on static template prompts. Moreover, they remain insufficient in modeling the complementary information between images and text. To address these issues, this article proposes a two-agent prior-guided multimodal network (TPMNet) for cross-scene HSI classification. First, a cross-domain semantic modeling mechanism guided by dual-agent priors is introduced. In this mechanism, source-domain and target-domain LLMs generate their respective prior texts. These priors are updated using similarity relationships with source-domain and target-domain image features, together with a memory-guided mechanism. As a result, dynamic textual representations with cross-domain perception capability are obtained. Second, a bidirectional multimodal cross-domain feature alignment and enhancement (BMAE) strategy is designed. Bidirectional cross-modal attention interactions are introduced between images and text to capture complementary discriminative representations across modalities. Meanwhile, a gating mechanism is adopted to select features that are highly relevant to the task, thereby improving the effectiveness of multimodal cross-domain features. Finally, a multiview consistency constraint learning (MCCL) method is proposed. Multilevel augmented views are constructed for target-domain samples. Multiple classifiers are designed to enforce joint consistency across different views, which enhances the classification capability of the model on target-domain data. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves better performance than seven advanced algorithms on multiple cross-scene hyperspectral classification tasks.
author: Ronghua Shang, Chi Wang, Jingyi Ding, Jie Feng

title: Label-Efficient Hyperspectral Image Change Detection via Multiscale Self-Distillation
content: Methods based on deep learning have achieved remarkable success in hyperspectral image change detection (HSI-CD). However, the high dependence on massive labeled data and the computational complexity of state-of-the-art models pose significant challenges, particularly in scenarios with extreme label scarcity. To address these issues, a multiscale self-distillation change detection (MSDistillCD) framework is proposed. In the proposed framework, two core modules are designed to extract robust features and enforce consistency under limited supervision. First, a multiscale feature extraction module (MSFEM) constructs subpatches aligned at the center from a fixed maximum patch and generates inputs with explicit difference information. A shared convolutional neural network (CNN) backbone with dual global aggregation is then employed to capture embeddings that remain robust across scales. Subsequently, a self-distillation classification module (SDCM) is utilized to facilitate knowledge transfer within the network. Unlike conventional distillation settings, the smallest-scale branch is treated as the primary branch and guides the larger-scale auxiliary branches through temperature-scaled self-distillation, providing additional regularization during training while allowing efficient inference with a single branch. Experimental results on benchmark HSI datasets demonstrate that MSDistillCD achieves the best overall accuracy (OA),  $\kappa \times 100$ , and  $F1$  across all three datasets, while maintaining robust performance even with extremely limited training samples (e.g., 0.1%). The source code of the proposed MSDistillCD will be released at https://github.com/zhangyuan1698-sketch/MSDistillCD
author: Zhiyuan Zhang, Zhijing Ye, Chengyong Zheng, Jie Li, Qiangqiang Yuan, Jiangtao Peng

title: Zero-Shot Multidegraded Hyperspectral Image Restoration via Intrinsic Image Decomposition
content: Hyperspectral images (HSIs) are often simultaneously degraded by spatial downsampling, complex noise contamination, and pixel loss during acquisition, resulting in spatial blurring and spectral distortion that severely hinder quantitative analysis and downstream applications. Most existing HSI restoration methods are designed for single degradation scenarios and heavily rely on paired supervision, which limits their applicability in unseen extreme environments where ground truth is unavailable. To address these challenges, this article proposes an unsupervised zero-shot HSI restoration (ZSHR) method based on intrinsic image decomposition (IID), grounded in physical imaging principles. Specifically, an HSI is modeled as the multiplicative interaction between reflectance and shading components, and the restoration under multiple degradations is reformulated as a joint estimation problem of intrinsic components under physical consistency constraints. This physics-driven decoupling allows the model to isolate inherent material properties from environmental illumination factors, ensuring high spectral fidelity in extreme scenarios. Accordingly, an end-to-end optimization framework is developed to jointly perform denoising and super-resolution (SR) reconstruction. By incorporating intrinsic consistency constraints between reflectance and shading, frequency-guided feature modulation, and panchromatic-guided cross-modal spatial fidelity constraints, the proposed method achieves high-quality HSI restoration without any external supervision. Extensive experiments on multiple public remote sensing datasets and challenging lunar in situ hyperspectral data demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing approaches in terms of spectral fidelity, spatial detail preservation, and downstream classification and unmixing performance.
author: Huaiyuan Wang, Jiansheng Wang, Fanli Lin, Kun Ding, Zhiping He, Qingli Li

title: Mining Heterogeneous Advantages via Feature Purification and Recombination for Multimodal Object Detection
content: Visible-infrared (IR) image fusion constitutes a pivotal paradigm for achieving all-weather robust object detection. However, its performance gains are frequently impeded by cross-modal semantic heterogeneity. This issue degrades representation quality in two primary ways. First, heterogeneous noises (e.g., thermal artifacts and shadows) induce severe feature contamination. Second, modality-specific advantages are often diluted. Due to heterogeneous feature representations, targets that are salient in only a single modality are frequently suppressed by invalid information from the other, ultimately leading to missed detections. Addressing these issues, we propose a novel framework for mining heterogeneous advantages via feature purification and recombination for multimodal object detection, termed FPR-Net. To this end, a cross-adversarial heterogeneous noise suppression (CAHN) mechanism is designed to facilitate feature purification. By mining the untainted semantic advantages of the complementary modality, CAHN dynamically guides the noise-corrupted modality to achieve robust semantic clarity. Furthermore, a saliency-guided feature recombination (SGFR) strategy is proposed to mitigate the dilution of modality-specific advantages. SGFR uses local response deviation to construct spatial saliency priors and enhance task-relevant components. By disentangling and recombining these features, it systematically mines heterogeneous advantages. Extensive experiments on four public datasets demonstrate that FPR-Net achieves significant performance gains in both remote sensing and natural scenes. In particular, FPR-Net achieves an  $\text {mAP}_{50}$  of 81.5% on the DroneVehicle dataset and 83.0% on the VEDAI dataset.
author: Yuhao Du, Zhanchao Huang, Junjie Wang, Li Wang, Aiguo Fei

title: GMSMO: Multiobjective Evolutionary Adversarial Attacks for Remote Sensing Images
content: The rapid deployment of on-orbit edge computing infrastructures, exemplified by recent initiatives to establish space-based data centers, has significantly accelerated the real-time application of remote sensing (RS) intelligence. However, this advancement exposes deep neural networks (DNNs) deployed in space to severe security threats from adversarial attacks, where imperceptible perturbations can mislead model predictions. Existing attack paradigms frame adversarial generation as a single-objective optimization problem constrained within a rigid ball, which suffers from limited decision boundaries and struggles to reconcile the conflicting objectives of adversarial transferability and visual imperceptibility. To this end, we propose a novel gradient-guided multiscale multiobjective optimization (GMSMO) framework. Specifically, we reformulate the attack generation as a balancing problem between two conflicting objectives: maximizing classification error while minimizing perturbation magnitude. This approach allows us to identify a set of optimal tradeoff solutions in which no single solution can improve one objective without compromising the other. To overcome the curse of dimensionality prevalent in pixel-level evolutionary search, GMSMO integrates the global exploration capacity of evolutionary algorithms with directional gradient-based priors. The core of this framework is the proposed multiscale momentum mutation (MSMM) operator, which extracts gradient information from surrogate models at varying scales to construct momentum-based trajectories. This mechanism effectively directs the optimization toward robust adversarial regions. Extensive experiments on standard optical RS datasets demonstrate that GMSMO generates a diverse set of adversarial examples (AEs) that achieve state-of-the-art transferability against advanced DNNs while maintaining superior visual quality compared to existing single-objective attack methods.
author: Xiaochuan Gao, Qianlong Dang, Baosheng Li, Tao Zhan, Maoguo Gong

title: GPCNet: Grid-Parallel Compact Network With Kernel-Adaptive Feature Fusion for Semantic Segmentation of High-Resolution UAV Imagery
content: In recent years, encoder–decoder architectures have driven remarkable progress in remote sensing semantic segmentation. However, achieving both high accuracy and computational efficiency for high-resolution UAV imagery remains challenging. For Vision Transformer (ViT)-based models, the quadratic computational and memory complexity of self-attention with respect to the number of tokens becomes prohibitive for large-scale UAV imagery. In addition, complex scenes with rich textures and fine-grained structures often exhibit significant intraclass appearance variations, which may degrade feature consistency and lead to object misclassification and boundary misalignment. To address these challenges, this article proposes GPCNet, an efficient semantic segmentation framework for high-resolution UAV imagery. First, we introduce foresight encoder sparsification (FES), which constructs a compact sparse encoder by evaluating parameter importance and removing redundant parameters prior to training. Second, we propose a grid-parallel encoding with stage-end semantic exchange (GPE-SSE) strategy to significantly reduce the computational cost of ViT-based encoders for high-resolution images while maintaining long-range semantic dependencies through cross-grid information exchange. Finally, a kernel-adaptive feature fusion (KAFF) module is designed for the semantic decoder, which generates spatially variable low-pass kernels (LPKs), high-pass kernels (HPKs), and dynamic dilated kernels (DDKs) to adaptively modulate high-frequency details and contextual receptive fields, thereby improving intraclass feature consistency and segmentation accuracy. The experimental results on three public high-resolution UAV image datasets demonstrate that our method maintains competitive segmentation accuracy while substantially improving inference efficiency. Specifically, with the compact MiT-B2 as the encoder, our GPCNet-P achieves 72.32% and 81.31% mIoU on the UAVid and VDD test sets, respectively, while reducing encoder parameters by 40% and the total FLOPs by 71.3% compared to the dense encoder. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/Memoristor/GPCNet
author: Changjian Deng, Jian Cheng, Zhiguo Yang, Yijie Zhang, Ziying Xia, Zijing Zhou, Nyima Tashi

title: Urban Dynamics Unveiled: Prompt-Driven Building Fine-Grained Change Detection
content: Building fine-grained change detection (BFCD) aims to identify the concrete change statuses of changed buildings. Despite its importance, BFCD has received limited attention, with few specialized models and benchmark datasets available. In this work, we construct a manually annotated BFCD dataset, termed UEDC-BFCD, to advance research in this direction. It introduces three statuses of changed buildings: disappeared, newly appeared, and replaced regions. Meanwhile, it encompasses multiple event types, including Urban Expansion, natural Disasters, and regional Conflicts. In addition, a new prompt-driven change detector (PromptCD) is developed, tailored for BFCD. First, we introduce the concept of single-temporal change embedding (STCE), enabling the differentiation of changed buildings from unchanged regions in the single-temporal image. PromptCD combines bi-temporal absolute difference representations with single-temporal features to form STCE. Then, we develop a prompt-guided transformer decoder (PGTD). It employs two learnable prompts to interact with the multilevel STCEs during decoding, thus refining the STCEs and modeling the spatiotemporal correlation. In particular, PGTD is computationally economical, ensuring the efficiency of the model. Finally, the change statuses of buildings are determined by combining the changed regions of buildings in the pretemporal and post-temporal images. Extensive experiments conducted on the UEDC-BFCD dataset, its urban expansion-focused subset UE-BFCD, as well as two existing datasets, demonstrate that PromptCD not only achieves superior performance but also maintains competitive complexity.
author: Mingwei Zhang, Jiawei Ren, Jingtao Hu, Weiping Ni, Junzheng Wu, Qi Wang

title: Frequency-Inspired Contrastive Feature Perturbation for Remote Sensing Semantic Segmentation
content: Semantic segmentation models for remote sensing images (RSIs) trained under the pretraining–fine-tuning paradigm commonly suffer from limited generalization. From a frequency-domain perspective, we identify the inherent low-frequency bias in deep neural networks as an important contributing factor. Such bias drives pretrained models to overrely on low-frequency appearance statistics and weakens the transfer of high-frequency structural cues. Through spectral response analysis across representative pretraining paradigms, we observe that the segment anything model (SAM)’s prompt-driven pretraining better preserves high-frequency structural cues, offering a favorable initialization; however, low-frequency bias may still be reinforced during fine-tuning as the model fits domain-specific style statistics. To address this issue, we propose frequency-inspired contrastive feature perturbation for SAM (CFP-SAM). This frequency-aware fine-tuning framework introduces a learnable low-frequency perturbation (LLFP) module into SAM’s encoder feature space. CFP-SAM jointly maximizes style discrepancy and enforces semantic consistency to suppress low-frequency style dependence and promote transferable structural representations. Extensive experiments on four public benchmarks show that CFP-SAM improves in-domain segmentation accuracy and source-only cross-domain generalization without introducing additional inference overhead. The code is available at https://github.com/wudi-ldd/CFP-SAM
author: Dongsheng Li, Pingting Hao, Xinyuan Guo, Huijie Zhang, Yiming Lin, Tong Gao

title: D2M-DETR: Differential Decoupling and Multiscale Dynamic Modeling for Remote Sensing Small Object Detection
content: In recent years, small object detection in remote sensing images has been widely applied in many fields, yet it still faces several serious challenges. On one hand, small objects inherently have weak features and are easily disturbed by complex backgrounds. On the other hand, small objects in remote sensing images are typically densely distributed and often accompanied by occlusion, which easily leads to missed detections and false positives. To tackle these challenges, we introduce an end-to-end detection network named  $\text {D}^{2}$ M-DETR, which integrates differential decoupling and multiscale dynamic modeling. The overall network comprises the differential decoupled salient features (DDSFs) strategy and the multiscale dynamic spatial context modeling (MDSCM) module. The DDSF strategy employs a dual-branch backbone for global and local feature extraction. It then applies differential decoupling to separate and enhance unique and basic features, effectively suppressing background interference and improving the discriminability of small objects. The MDSCM module jointly constructs multiscale dynamic local focus and multidirectional global spatial modeling, and enhances interactions among multiscale contextual information. This enables explicit modeling of structural priors and semantic relationships of small objects in densely occluded scenes. Our  $\text {D}^{2}$ M-DETR achieves excellent detection performance on multiple remote sensing datasets, validating the efficacy of the proposed algorithm. The source code is available at https://github.com/Xidian-AIGroup190726/DDMDETR
author: Wenping Ma, Zhenyu Hu, Hao Zhu, Xuqiang Lv, Weiwei Hou, Mengru Ma

title: LDI-3DGS: Structurally Robust 3-D Gaussian Splatting Driven by UAV-Borne LiDAR Depth and Intensity Priors
content: 3-D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) has demonstrated outstanding performance in novel view synthesis and 3-D scene reconstruction. While 3DGS can technically be optimized from random initialization, achieving high-quality and scale-accurate reconstruction in large-scale scenes still relies heavily on sparse structure-from-motion (SfM) point clouds for reliable initialization. In these expansive urban environments featuring weak-texture regions, purely visual SfM frequently fails to provide robust and scale-accurate geometric priors. Consequently, Gaussian primitives lack sufficient high-frequency visual constraints, causing them to undergo unconstrained splitting and erroneous cloning. This often leads to severe structural collapse, floaters, and rendering blur. To overcome these limitations, we propose LDI-3DGS, a structurally robust scene reconstruction pipeline driven by dual physical priors. First, a light detection and ranging (LiDAR)-constrained joint bundle adjustment is formulated to rigorously register images into a drift-free absolute physical coordinate system, effectively eliminating scale drift. Second, dense spatial depth maps serve as geometric anchors to pull the Gaussian field onto actual physical surfaces. Furthermore, to address the inherent rendering blur in weak-texture regions, we innovatively leverage LiDAR reflection intensity to resolve the shape-radiance ambiguity. By formulating a joint color-intensity radiance field and enforcing an intensity-guided pruning constraint, our framework introduces a robust physical material prior to suppress erroneous Gaussian cloning. Extensive experiments on real-world urban datasets demonstrate that LDI-3DGS better preserves geometric and textural details, including road markings and highly reflective structures. Moreover, our framework improves absolute 3-D geometric accuracy and  $F1$ -scores while reducing the total number of Gaussian primitives by approximately 23% relative to the baseline, ultimately delivering a structurally robust, compact, and physically accurate 3-D scene representation.
author: Tianjiao Wang, Qingzhou Mao, Zhixin Duan, Xuran He

title: Dual-Context Joint Representation for Near-Infrared Geo-Localization in Urban Environments
content: Visual geo-localization seeks to enable autonomous aircraft positioning in GNSS-denied environments through large-scale image retrieval. Most existing methods, however, primarily rely on visible light images and are thus inherently sensitive to illumination changes and adverse weather conditions. Near-infrared (NIR) images offer superior environmental robustness but lack well-established benchmarks and specialized retrieval algorithms. To bridge this gap, we introduce NIR-cities, the first urban-scale benchmark for NIR aerial-to-satellite geo-localization. Unlike previous datasets, it features unaligned queries and continuous spatial coverage, simulating nadir-view aerial queries. Building on this, we propose a novel dual-context joint representation (DCJR) network specifically designed for NIR images. DCJR decouples the image representation into salient and environmental contexts via saliency-guided patch encoding (SPE). A dual-context enhancement (DCE) module then adaptively fuses these dual cues to address local ambiguities. Finally, region-prototype aggregation (RPA) distills the features through learnable prototypes, resulting in a discriminative and compact global descriptor. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DCJR significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, attaining a remarkable R@1 of 73.44% while achieving a favorable accuracy-efficiency tradeoff.
author: Tengda Zhang, Yunzhou Zhang, Li Wang, Guolu Chen, Guiyuan Wang, Wei Liu

title: Retrieval of Cirrus Cloud Extinction Coefficient From LiDAR Observation by Considering the Coherent Backscatter Enhancement of Ice Crystals
content: The backscattering intensity of an ice crystal is typically stronger than near-backscattering intensity due to the coherent backscatter enhancement (CBE) in single scattering, but the effect of the CBE-induced backscattering peak has not been accounted for in forward radiative transfer models of variational LiDAR retrieval algorithms. In this study, the scattering properties of ice crystals are calculated using the improved geometric optics method (IGOM), where the CBE effect is quantified using a paired ray-tracing technique. Then, the effect of CBE on the near-backscattering phase function of ice crystals is applied to a fast-forward model [fast LiDAR and radar multiple-scattering model (FMM)], and the results of the revised model are validated using a Monte Carlo radiative transfer model. Subsequently, a variational method based on the revised fast-forward model is used to retrieve the extinction coefficient of cirrus clouds from Cloud–Aerosol LiDAR and Infrared Pathfinder Satellite Observations (CALIPSO), when the off-nadir viewing angle is 3° to avoid specular reflection from horizontally oriented ice crystals. The results show that the CBE-induced backscattering peak has remarkable impact on the retrieval of extinction coefficient profile, and the consideration of CBE improves the consistency between simulated LiDAR backscatter and collocated passive and active satellite observations (8% reduction in the RMSE for transparent cirrus).
author: He Huang, Chen Zhou, Lei Bi, Qingming Wang

title: Efficient Unsupervised Deep Band Selection for Hyperspectral Imagery: A Comparative Study With Mamba-Based Classification
content: Band selection is a critical step in processing hyperspectral imagery (HSI); reducing input dimensionality allows models to mitigate redundancy, enhance computational efficiency, and improve learning accuracy. Efficient unsupervised deep-learning-based band selection methods have recently garnered immense attention due to their advanced feature representation capabilities. The existing literature shows there is a broader and more general line of research regarding feature selection, from which some recent deep learning-based HSI band selection methods have drawn inspiration. This work is a comparative study focusing on efficient unsupervised deep-learning-based HSI band selection methods, most of which are adapted from the general feature selection. A benchmarking analysis was conducted in terms of downstream classification performance and computation cost, on six state-of-the-art efficient unsupervised HSI band selection methods. Classification experiments were carried out using three publicly available remote sensing datasets and three classifiers—MambaHSI, HyPyraMamba, and a Support Vector Machine. This work provides a unified comparison of these efficient unsupervised methods for HSI band selection and investigates the use of Mamba-based classification in this context.
author: Jacqueline Liu, Kara Combs, Jayson Boubin

title: Separating Sea Ice and Open Water in Sentinel-1 EW Imagery Based on a Model-Informed Threshold for Backscatter Intensity Decay Rates With Incidence Angle
content: Combining backscatter modeling with observations from Sentinel-1 (S1) wide-swath imagery, we derive a threshold separating sea ice and open water based on their incidence angle (IA) slopes for HH-polarized backscatter intensity in winter conditions. Backscatter from C-band synthetic aperture radar (SAR) over open water is here modeled through a geophysical model function for wind speeds up to 25 m/s. Averaged linear slopes are estimated from the geophysical modeled backscatter across the full scene as well as in local IA bins to account for curvature. IA slopes from different sea ice types across multiple Arctic study sights are found in literature in addition to regression analysis on SAR backscatter from selected S1 scenes. Results indicate that −0.40 dB/1$^\circ$ is a suitable threshold distinguishing ice from open water with uniform wind conditions. To demonstrate the threshold, and the potential for automatically assigning physics based class labels (sea ice and open water), we apply it to results from unsupervised clustering showcasing high spatial resolution ice–water maps. Challenges related to clustering and local wind gradients are further explored and discussed.
author: Madeleine Östersund, Anthony P. Doulgeris, Johannes Lohse

title: LiteSVC-GCP: Global Context Prior-Enhanced Lightweight Neural Video Compression for Satellite Staring Video
content: Satellite staring video provides high-resolution, long-duration observations of local regions, but the resulting data volume and strict onboard computation budgets make efficient compression particularly challenging. Existing neural video compression (NVC) methods are mostly developed for generic natural videos and do not consider the distinct spatiotemporal statistics of satellite staring imagery. Their optical-flow-based motion branches and large contextual and entropy networks are therefore overdesigned for this scenario, leading to high FLOPs and memory usage that are difficult to accommodate in satellite environments and excessive relative to the underlying spatiotemporal redundancy. In this work, we first perform a modulewise parameter and complexity analysis of representative NVC architectures, revealing that motion, context, and entropy branches dominate the computation cost and exhibit strong feature redundancy. Guided by these observations and the spatiotemporal properties of staring video, we propose LiteSVC-global context prior (GCP), a lightweight, flow-free NVC framework tailored for satellite staring video. LiteSVC-GCP replaces dense computation modules with the proposed parameter-efficient LiteBlocks and adopts a simple context-based codec, substantially reducing model size and computation. In addition, a GCP module aggregates long-term scene information and fuses it with short-term reference features through a dual-mask mechanism, enabling the codec to better capture temporally varying regions while leveraging slowly changing scene content. Experiments on Jilin-1 and Carbonite-2 satellite videos demonstrate that LiteSVC-GCP outperforms the traditional H.265/HEVC codec on most sequences while using only 5.1 M parameters and roughly 5–$\text{6}\times$ fewer FLOPs than strong NVC baselines to achieve comparable or better rate–distortion performance.
author: Hao Qi, Fanyang Meng, Han Shen, Yangxuan Cheng, Zhongqiang Zhang, Ye Wang, Yongsheng Liang

title: Anomaly Detection of Space Targets From Terahertz ISAR Image Sequences With Dual-Branch Network
content: Dynamic anomaly detection of space targets is critical for space situational awareness. With the range-Doppler projection mechanism, inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) image sequences possess significant potential for interpreting abnormal dynamics of noncooperative targets. Previous studies on anomaly detection have primarily focused on low-frequency bands, neglecting the richer pixel-level details available in terahertz (THz) ISAR images. This article proposes an anomaly detection method utilizing THz ISAR image sequences, featuring a spatial-entropy dual-branch temporal classification network with Image Spatial Feature Extraction (ISFE) and Boundary-Guided Feature Fusion (BGFF) modules. The ISFE module employs a convolutional neural network (CNN) to automatically extract spatial features from ISAR image sequences. The BGFF module captures statistical features including image entropy and contrast for each frame, and integrates them into CNN feature maps in a structured spatial manner. Ultimately, the long short-term memory temporal modeling is applied to generate sequence classification results. Experimental results on the THz ISAR dataset demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed architecture.
author: Shuangshuang Hu, Qi Yang, Jun Yi, Kang Liu, Chenggao Luo, Hongqiang Wang

title: SSMFusion: A Large Vision Mamba Model With Adaptive Feature Disentanglement for Remote Sensing Spatiotemporal Fusion
content: Remote sensing spatiotemporal fusion aims to generate land surface observations with both high spatial and temporal resolution by integrating multisource satellite imagery, which is of great importance for applications, such as agricultural monitoring and environmental analysis. However, existing mainstream methods still face challenges in modeling long-range spatiotemporal dependencies and capturing high-frequency abrupt land-cover changes. Moreover, current studies lack explicit modeling of the relatively stable shared information and the dynamic differential information caused by land-cover changes during the temporal evolution of remote sensing imagery, which limits fusion accuracy. To tackle these challenges, this article introduces SSMFusion, a spatiotemporal feature fusion framework for remote sensing that explicitly models both “common” and “specific” characteristics via state-space equations. First, a hybrid hierarchical feature extraction module is designed. This module utilizes state-space equations to encode global-scale contextual correlations while maintaining linear computational efficiency. Meanwhile, spatial attention mechanisms and dynamic convolution are introduced to enhance local textures and edge details. Second, an adaptive spatiotemporal fusion module is developed to disentangle and effectively fuse stable shared features and dynamic change features under the guidance of spectral and temporal variation information, thereby improving spatiotemporal reconstruction in complex land-surface scenarios. Furthermore, to alleviate the lack of high-quality validation data in agricultural phenology applications, we construct the California Central Valley (CCV) dataset, which covers typical agricultural ecological zones in CCV, USA. Experimental results on two public datasets and the newly constructed CCV dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior quantitative performance over existing mainstream methods.
author: Liuwei Bian, Xiaolong Xu, Zhanyang Xu, Haolong Xiang, Wanchun Dou, Bayan Alabdullah, Muhammad Attique Khan, Muhammad Bilal

title: Pathfinder: Efficient Snow Depth, Stratigraphy, and Uncertainty Determination From Radar Measurements
content: Snow strongly influences the climate system through its albedo and insulating properties, while also representing a critical freshwater resource. Yet, its spatial and temporal variability remain poorly constrained due to limitations of in situ and satellite observations. Unoccupied aerial vehicle (UAV)-mounted surface-penetrating radars provide a solution for high-resolution snow surveys, but their data are often difficult to interpret because of variable flight conditions, which, combined with the complicated microwave interactions with snow, result in complex noise and signal patterns. We present Pathfinder, an open-source algorithm for automatic detection of snow interfaces in radar echograms. The method formulates interface tracking as a path-finding problem, combining cost maps derived from reflection strength, ridge detection, and horizontal continuity, and solves it using an efficient dynamic-programming scheme. Pathfinder retrieves the air–snow and snow–ground (or snow–ice) interfaces, and can additionally identify internal layers when present. Validation against coincident in situ, probe-derived snow depth measurements shows an accuracy of snow depth retrievals with R$^{2}$ = 0.96 and RMSE = 8 cm. The algorithm is computationally efficient, enabling real-time application during UAV surveys. Pathfinder was developed for the ultrawide-band snow sensor (UWiBaSS) from NORCE Research but we show it to be transferable across different UAV-mounted and ground-based radar systems. Case studies from Svalbard, the Alps, and polar sea ice demonstrate its robustness across diverse, but mostly dry snow conditions. Pathfinder advances UAV-borne radar as a practical tool for snow depth and stratigraphy mapping by providing an efficient, and operational interface detection method. Consequently, it can support both scientific research and in-the-field decision-making.
author: Torbjörn Kagel, Aart C. Stuurman, Anna Siebenbrunner, Robert Ricker, Rolf-Ole R. Jenssen

title: Detection of Non-stand-Replacing Cuttings Using Satellite Image Time Series With a Kalman Filter
content: Detection of nonstand-replacing disturbances is becoming highly important for forest monitoring. Methods to detect severe, stand-replacing disturbances are increasingly mature. On the other hand, nonstand-replacing disturbances, though less severe, may cover large forest areas and thus pose an important monitoring problem, yet they remain difficult to detect in optical satellite image time series. The often very subtle change signals can usually be detected only for a brief time period, and the signal is often obscured by noise. In this study, we tested three detection algorithms that consider abruptness of and prior information about spectral changes to varying degrees. These detectors, in combination with a Kalman filter (KF), were applied to detect both stand-replacing and nonstand-replacing anthropogenic forest disturbances in six study sites throughout Finland. Clearcuts and heavy thinnings were easily detected without application of advanced detectors, but low intensity thinnings were detectable only by using both prior information and the assumption that changes are abrupt. The best detector achieved an F$_{1}$-score of 0.67 for thinnings detection, compared to $< $0.56 for other detectors as well as the stochastic continuous change detection (S-CCD) method and the European Forest Disturbance Atlas (EFDA). In clearcuts, the three detectors we tested performed equally well as S-CCD and EFDA. The results indicate the potential of using an informative Bayesian approach in detecting nonstand-replacing disturbances with optical satellite image time series.
author: Daniel Schraik, Aku Ursin, Petteri Packalen

title: PstpNet: Dual-Branch Physics-Guided U-Net With Multiscale Spatiotemporal Disentanglement for Precipitation Nowcasting
content: Precipitation nowcasting remains challenging because precipitation systems exhibit strong nonlinear evolution, rapid development, and complex long-range spatiotemporal dependencies. Existing deep learning methods are still limited in characterizing precipitation dynamics and improving model interpretability. To address these limitations, we propose PstpNet, a physics-informed nowcasting model. Inspired by the continuity equation, PstpNet constructs an advection-residual decomposition framework, in which a motion branch and a residual branch separately model advective transport and nonconservative intensity changes. Multiscale feature fusion is further introduced to enhance the representation of precipitation structures at different spatial scales. In addition, the TM module embeds historical temporal evolution information into the physical decomposition process, while the physics-guided fusion module adaptively coordinates advection and intensity-residual processes, thereby improving spatiotemporal consistency and physical interpretability in long-lead forecasting. Experimental results on the KNMI-NL50 and SEVIR datasets show that PstpNet achieves the best or near-best performance across threshold-based metrics, with strong high-intensity detection performance at the 10 mm/h rainfall threshold on KNMI-NL50 and the VIL 181 threshold on SEVIR.
author: Kai Xie, Bo Yin, Yue-Ting Sun, Zhaoyan Zhu, Yiyun Guo

title: Effects of Seamounts and Islands and Reefs on Constructing Topography from SWOT Satellite Gravity Anomaly: A Case of South China Sea
content: High-resolution seafloor topography is essential for ensuring maritime navigation safety and providing data support for cutting-edge research in fields such as geodesy and geodynamics. Currently, marine gravity anomalies are the primary data source used in topography inversion. However, technical limitations in satellite altimetry result in insufficient accuracy of gravity models in reef regions; conventional inversion algorithms are mostly suitable for areas with gentle topography and perform inadequate in regions with significant undulations such as seamounts. To address these issues, this study employs the latest SWOT_03 gravity anomaly model and incorporates prior information from reef-shallow waters depth model and seamount morphology to develop a refined multisource data fusion algorithm for topography inversion that accounts for spatial heterogeneity. The algorithm is applied to South China Sea (SCS), a region characterized by widespread seamounts and reefs, and inversion experiments are conducted using both V32.1 gravity anomaly model and SWOT_03 gravity anomaly model. Results show that the inversion derived from the SWOT_03 model achieves a root mean square error (RMSE) error of 71.7 m when validated against ship soundings, compared to an RMSE of 99.1 m for a model constructed without integrating seamount and reef data. Moreover, the inversion results using SWOT_03 model yields a 14.6% improvement (71.7 m versus 84.0 m) compared to V32.1 model. Evaluated against the SRTM15+ and GEBCO_2024 topography models, the SWOT_03 enhanced inversion reduces RMSE by 51.4% (71.7 m versus 147.4 m) and 48% (71.7 m versus 136.8 m), respectively.
